title: Get Model Info (GGUF) (GGUF (llama.cpp), LLM, ML Model)
cap_description: Query metadata and capabilities of a GGUF model
documentation:
## Purpose

Returns metadata stored in a GGUF model file's header: architecture, parameter count, quantization type, context length, vocabulary size, and other configuration fields. Use this to inspect a model before using it in a pipeline.

## Inputs

A generation request JSON record with `request_type` set to `model_info` and the model spec to inspect.

## Outputs

A JSON object with model metadata fields extracted from the GGUF header.

## Notes

- No inference is run; this reads the GGUF file metadata only.
- Use this cap to verify that a model's context length and architecture are compatible with your pipeline before committing to a full inference run.
- For vocabulary extraction (needed by constrained generation), use [Get Model Vocabulary (GGUF)](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:gguf;in="media:llm-generation-request;json;record";llm;ml-model;op=llm_vocab;out="media:llm-vocab-response;json;record").

## Backend
The inference framework or runtime that loads and executes a model. Backend choice
determines weight format, hardware acceleration, and runtime characteristics. A media
URN that omits the backend tag is backend-agnostic — it accepts any backend.

GGUF is the llama.cpp container format. Quantised weights packaged into a single
file with embedded metadata. Runs efficiently on CPU and via Metal/CUDA acceleration.
Standard format for general-purpose LLM and embedding inference across hardware.

## Model task
The inference modality of a model. Model-task narrows what kind of inference cap a
model spec is suitable for: an LLM cannot serve transcription, a transcription model
cannot serve text generation. The task tag is part of the model-spec URN; it is set
by the cap declaring its model-spec input slot, not derived from the model file.

Causal language model for text generation and instruction following. Accepts a text
prompt and produces a text continuation, typically token-by-token via streaming.

## ML model
Marker indicating the cap invokes a machine-learning model. Inputs typically
include a model spec or model artifact; the cap is subject to model-resolution
and hardware-pressure policies.

The cap invokes a machine-learning model.
